column1: # Migrations that error when replayed against a fresh init/ build, with the reason.
# scripts/schema-drift-check.sh replays every migration onto a fresh init/ build and
# compares the result against init/ alone. These seven raise and do nothing. That is
# harmless only because init/ already carries their end state, which is exactly what the
# diff downstream proves - so this file records WHY each one fails, not merely that it does.
# The gate fails if a name or a reason changes, because a migration failing for a new cause
# is a different fact than a migration failing for an adjudicated one.
# None of them runs on a real instance. All seven are at or below the 20260809000001
# baseline cutoff, so an existing instance records them without replaying, and a fresh
# install gets its schema from init/ and records history without replaying either.
# Three causes:
#   init/ is ahead - the migration tries to change an object into a shape init/ already
#   surpassed. CREATE OR REPLACE cannot rename a parameter or change a return type, and a
#   policy cannot be created twice.
#   ownership - the gate runs as postgres. public objects are owned by supabase_admin and
#   realtime.messages by supabase_realtime_admin, so DDL against them is refused. The same
#   cause stops `supabase db push` after one migration when the CLI connects as postgres:
#   `ERROR: must be owner of relation invites (SQLSTATE 42501)`. Connect the CLI as the
#   owning role instead. self-host/bootstrap.sh already detects it in pick_db_role().
#   prod-only relation - public.pg_background_job is one of five tables production carries
#   that init/ does not. It is cruft, not schema, so init/ is right to lack it.
# Format: <filename>\t<first ERROR line>. RI_ConstraintTrigger OIDs are masked to * because
# they move whenever init/ changes.
